newsitem.title: USA: U.S. late spot prods edge lower following API data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. late spot prods edge lower following API data.

text.p: U.S. heating oil and gasoline prices slipped about 0.40 cent a gallon in after-hours ACCESS trade late Tuesday following API data showing significant builds during the prior week, players said.
The API data showed distillate stocks swelling by 2.9 million barrels for the week ending January 3.
"It's a little strange. It's building in areas that don't do the market much good," one trader said, noting most of the distillate build was in the Midwest and Gulf Coast.

More specifically, heating oil stocks grew by 1.9 million barrels in the U.S., including 1.4 million barrels in the Gulf Coast. But they grew by only 400,000 in the East Coast -- the world's largest heating oil market -- according to the API data.
"The market will take the overall distillate build as bearish because it was only expecting an extra one million barrels," an East Coast trader said.
"But it won't be too bearish because you can only move so many barrels to the East Coast from a logistical standpoint," he added.
